page.overview:
What is Ella?

Ella is a miniature doll-like animatronic who first appears as the main antagonist of 1:35 A.M., the first story in the book of the same name, and then as a cameo character in the epilogue of Fazbear Frights 5: Bunny Call.

Ella's appearance seems to be relatively similar to the illustrations of her novel trilogy counterpart. She is about two feet tall with brown curly hair, big dark eyes, and plump pink cheeks, which reminds Delilah of the baby she envisioned having one day. Ella also has thick lashes and baby-soft "skin." Her pretty baby face is partially shadowed by her blue hat, with its wide brim fringed in pink ruffles. Ella wears a puffy-sleeved, 1980s-era bright blue full-skirted dress with pink ruffled trim and a big bow around the waist. Because she is electronic, she is heavier than she looks. Ella has a small digital clock embedded in her chest, which can be activated by pressing a sequence of little buttons on her round belly.

When at the garage sale in 1:35 A.M., a bright pink tag reading “My name is Ella,” and an instructional booklet was hung around Ella’s wrist at the garage sale. Pinned to her dress is a note explaining that only the alarm clock works. There was a little white price tag stuck to the back of Ella's neck.

Ella is a high-tech electronic doll manufactured by Fazbear Entertainment. She was a "helper doll" designed to do a number of tasks, such as keeping time and serving as an alarm clock, managing appointments, keeping track of lists, taking photos, reading stories, singing songs, and serving drinks. Ella could also test the pH level in water and do personality assessments when the owner answered her programmed list of 200 questions. The doll Delilah finds, however, can only function as an alarm clock.
